The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

‘Wow, it’s a real discovery’: Claude cracks a 25-year NSA number mystery. Numbers the spy agency handed over in the 1990s, long suspected of hiding a backdoor, turn out to have come from a basic computer program. Bitcoin was never on that list, and its quantum problem hasn’t gone anywhere. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Satoshi-era bitcoin faces a bigger quantum threat after Google’s new Willow breakthrough. Google says its Willow chip can prepare the special quantum states needed for advanced calculations with about 40 times fewer errors, reducing one of the hardware bottlenecks behind any future attempt to crack bitcoin wallets. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Big Tech's AI auditors will only see what they're shown. If the White House accord's audits are going to be worth anything, auditors should be able to choose what they test, writes Samuel Vance-Law, head of research at the Decentralization Research Center. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Traders will soon be able to bet on whether Coinbase, Robinhood and Marathon will hit their targets. Your day-ahead look for Oct. 16, 2026 Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Circle targets 40 new markets as stablecoin demand grows globally. The stablecoin issuer’s CEO Jerermy Allaire told Reuters demand for digital dollars is growing across Asia, Africa and Latin America as banks and payment firms. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Quantum Alliance forms amid warnings 6.4 million bitcoin face future quantum threat. Nine crypto companies launched the Quantum Alliance to jointly prepare for quantum attacks, but they disagree on when the threat will arrive and whether vulnerable BTC should be frozen. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $81,600 with a -0.73% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $2,431.48 with a -0.87% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

items.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs Lost $391 Million in a Day. Only XRP ETFs Took Money In.
items.description:
Investors withdrew a significant $391 million from Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) and Ethereum (CRYPTO:ETH) exchange-traded funds (ETFs), according to SoSoValue. Bitcoin ETFs lost $261.46 million, while Ethereum ETFs saw outflows of $129.51 million. In contrast, XRP (CRYPTO:XRP) funds experienced a positive shift, with XRP ETF inflows reaching $740,414, making it the only fund group among the four major cryptocurrencies to see any inflow. [...] Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs shed a combined $391 million in a single day, Bitcoin's second-largest October outflow.
 XRP ETFs recorded just $740,414 in inflows after three straight inactive sessions, a figure amounting to less than 0.3% of Bitcoin's outflow.
 XRP fund holders sit at an average loss, with net assets of $1.51 billion against $1.80 billion in cumulative investment since launch. [...] Ethereum funds also faced a setback, shedding $129.51 million the same day, adding to selling pressure on the two largest cryptocurrencies. Meanwhile, Solana (CRYPTO:SOL) funds fell slightly, shedding $1.29 million. Although small, this marks the ninth out of ten October sessions in which Solana funds have faced outflows, highlighting an ongoing trend.

items.title: US Crypto Policy Tracker Regulatory Developments
items.description:
On April 4, 2025, the SEC’s Division of Corporation Finance (the Staff) published a Statement on Stablecoins clarifying that in the Staff’s view the offer and sale of certain dollar-backed stablecoins does not involve an offer and sale of securities requiring registration under the US federal securities laws (the Stablecoin Statement). The Stablecoin Statement specifically addresses stablecoins that are designed to maintain a stable value relative to the US dollar (USD) on a one-for-one basis, [...] On December 16, 2025, the FDIC issued a notice of proposed rulemaking (the Proposal) to implement Section 5 of the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for US Stablecoins Act (GENIUS Act). The GENIUS Act, enacted by Congress in July 2025, created a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins whereby a subsidiary of an insured depository institution could be approved to issue payment stablecoins.

Read more on Latham’sGlobal Fintech & Digital Assets Blog. [...] On April 1, 2026, the Treasury issued a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM), seeking public comment related to its implementation of the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for US Stablecoins Act (the GENIUS Act), a comprehensive framework for the federal regulation of payment stablecoins enacted on July 18, 2025.

Read more on Latham's Global Fintech & Digital Assets Blog.

# Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP Price Predictions Today: Why Is Crypto Falling?

Coin Gabbar

Coin Gabbar@coin\_gabbar\_·

The crypto market took a step back today. The total market cap fell to $2.76 trillion, down 0.60% in the past 24 hours. Trading volume sits at $94.41 billion.

Bitcoin slipped to $78,062.80. Ethereum eased to $2,470.13. XRP dropped to $1.38. Most coins are red today, but the drop is mild, not a crash.

### Why is Crypto Market Down Today? [...] Ethereum trades at $2,472.04 today, down 1.80%. The coin has been stuck between $2,400 and $2,550 for over a week now.

Retail selling and a slowdown in demand from bigger buyers seem to be the main reasons for the sideways action.

Near-term resistance sits around $2,520 to $2,530. That level has rejected price several times in recent weeks. Each retest without a sharp rejection tends to weaken resistance over time, which raises the odds of an eventual breakout. [...] Markets are now pricing in a 60.4% chance of a rate hike at the September 16 Fed meeting, up from 39.6% odds of no change.

A month ago, the odds were close to a coin flip. Now, the market thinks a hike is more likely than not. Higher rates usually mean less money flowing into risk assets like crypto.

### Is the crypto market in fear or greed right now?

The Fear & Greed Index shows a score of 69 today. That puts the market in Greed territory.
